title: Cellular Automata: Order from Simple Rules
category_reason: Cellular automata as a model of computation and complexity (Wolfram classes, Turing completeness, chaos); no ML/NN application
thesis: Simple, local, deterministic update rules on a lattice of cells generate chaos, emergence, self-organization, and even universal computation, making cellular automata a bridge between simple rules and complex behavior.
key_claims: Elementary CAs have 2^8 = 256 rules from the 8 possible 3-cell neighborhoods; Wolfram's Class III (Rule 30) is chaotic and Class IV (Rule 110) sits at the edge of chaos
Conway's Game of Life (1970) is Turing complete — it can compute anything a computer can
Rule 110 is proven Turing complete; Rule 90 yields the Sierpinski triangle (XOR of neighbors); Rule 184 models traffic flow; Rule 30 was used by Wolfram as a PRNG
Chaos in CAs is sensitive dependence on initial conditions: flipping one cell changes the long-term evolution, tracked by a Lyapunov-like divergence rate and Shannon entropy
Chaotic (Class III) rules drive Shannon entropy toward its maximum, ordered (Class I/II) rules toward 0, and edge-of-chaos (Class IV) rules show intermediate entropy
The forest-fire CA demonstrates self-organized criticality: the system relaxes to a critical state where fire sizes follow a power law
visualizations: 1D ECA evolution canvas (vanilla JS canvas 2D) for rules 30/110/90/184 with rule-table display
Conway's Game of Life canvas with loadable patterns (glider, blinker, pulsar, Gosper gun, R-pentomino, acorn)
side-by-side chaos/sensitivity canvas showing Hamming-distance growth and a Lyapunov bar
entropy-over-time plot (canvas) per rule class
forest-fire CA canvas (tree-growth + lightning sliders)
internal_tensions: The 'edge of chaos' / complexity-from-simple-rules claim is asserted as the takeaway but not argued as a theory of computation; the file never links CAs to neural nets (a contrast with the math-for-AI cluster in this corpus)
The 'Lyapunov-like exponent' is a heuristic (log of late/early Hamming difference), not a true dynamical-systems Lyapunov exponent

title: Finnegans Wake
category_reason: A single-canvas game retelling chapters of Joyce's Finnegans Wake as playable vignettes; literature/game, no ML
thesis: A no-HUD, full-window canvas 'game' that walks through nine chapters of Joyce's Finnegans Wake — each rendered as a small playable vignette with its own palette — ending in a dissolve-to-white that loops back to the opening, mirroring the book's circular structure.
key_claims: Maps Finnegans Wake's sections to nine playable chapters (fw00–fw08): the fall from the ladder, HCE's Phoenix Park rumor, the pub/trial, Shem the Penman writing ink on his body, ALP's letter down the Liffey, the Norwegian ship, the quiz, Shaun's barrel-sermon, and ALP dissolving as the river reaches the sea
The whole is a cycle: chapter 8 (ALP dissolving, dawn) fades to white and returns to chapter 0, enacting the book's circular 'fall / wake' structure
Each chapter is a distinct micro-genre (collect, dodge, draw, steer, balance, catch) keyed to a per-chapter color palette matched to the section's mood
Input is mouse/touch plus WASD/arrows; the cursor is hidden and replaced by a custom dot; there is no on-screen text except in-canvas progress pips and a health bar
visualizations: single full-window canvas 2D game (vanilla JS): 9 chapter vignettes — crumbling tower/fall, park with spreading rumor rings and accusers, pub gavel-dodger, ink-trail body-drawing, scrolling river with gifts, ship/ice-berg dodging, falling-symbol quiz catcher, rotating barrel-sermon scroll, dissolving-particle sea
particle systems (gravity, life decay), screen-shake, and screen-fade chapter transitions
internal_tensions: There is essentially no fail/lose state (only the pub transitions on 0 health); 'completion' is defined by collection thresholds rather than challenge
It reduces Joyce's pun-dense, polyglot text to mood/palette/color per chapter — the linguistic play that is the actual Wake is entirely absent; this is visual metaphor, not the text
Chapter 8 is non-interactive (a timed dissolve), breaking the otherwise playable structure

title: Principal Bundles – Interaktives Lerntool
category_reason: Principal bundles / gauge theory applied to the fundamental forces (EM, weak, strong, gravity); math for physics, no ML
thesis: A principal bundle is a space carrying a full symmetry (Lie) group over each base point, and the real question is how those symmetries are globally twisted; that twist — the connection and its curvature — is exactly gauge physics (the EM potential, the field strength, and the Aharonov–Bohm effect).
key_claims: A Principal G-bundle has fiber = Lie group G acting freely and transitively on each fiber, base M = P/G, and is the 'mother bundle' from which every associated bundle P×_G F is built
A bundle is determined up to isomorphism by its transition functions g_ij satisfying the cocycle condition g_ij·g_jk·g_ki = e on triple overlaps
A connection is a 𝔤-valued 1-form ω; locally A_i = s_i*ω is the physics gauge potential, and curvature Ω = dω + ½[ω,ω] is the field strength
For U(1) electromagnetism the curvature F = dA is the EM field tensor, with gauge transformation A → A + ∂λ
Fundamental forces as connections: EM = U(1), weak = SU(2), strong QCD = SU(3) (8 gluons = dim su(3)), gravity = frame bundle with Lorentz group SO(3,1) and Riemann curvature
The Aharonov–Bohm effect: with F = 0 (flat connection) the holonomy exp(i∮A) = exp(iΦ/ℏ) can still be nontrivial — showing the gauge potential A, not only F, is physically real
Flat curvature (F = 0) does NOT imply a trivial bundle — holonomy can remain nontrivial
visualizations: cylinder vs Möbius-bundle intuition canvas with animated fiber transport (vanilla JS canvas 2D)
3D-projected torus (S¹×S¹) with a twist slider; Hopf fibration S¹→S³→S²; connection (horizontal/vertical) and parallel-transport/holonomy scenes
Aharonov–Bohm two-path interference canvas with phase circles and a flux slider
internal_tensions: Explicitly warns that 'flat' (F=0) ≠ 'trivial' — a common confusion the tool pushes against
Identifies the Hopf fibration as describing the magnetic-monopole bundle, a physics claim asserted without proof
The 'clock on a circle' analogy equates the U(1) fiber with a rotating clock hand, flattening the group action

title: Topological Data Analysis — Visual Explorer
category_reason: TDA (Vietoris-Rips, Mapper, Alpha, persistence) applied to generic point-cloud/shape data; ML appears only as a persistence-landscape use-case with no application to neural nets or embeddings
thesis: Topological data analysis extracts the shape of data — connected components, loops, voids — by building simplicial complexes filtered by a scale parameter, and summarizes them with invariants beyond barcodes: persistence landscapes, Euler characteristic curves, Reeb graphs, and the Mapper algorithm.
key_claims: Vietoris-Rips: connect points within distance ≤ 2ε and fill all cliques as simplices; as ε grows, components and loops are born and die (a filtration)

The Mapper algorithm (Singh, Mémoli, Carlsson 2007) projects data through a filter, covers the range with overlapping intervals, clusters each preimage, and builds a graph — a topological 'skeleton' revealing loops, branches, and flares
The Alpha complex is a subcomplex of the Delaunay triangulation (keep simplices with circumradius ≤ α), geometrically more faithful and cheaper than Vietoris-Rips in low dimensions

Persistence landscapes (Bubenik 2015): each interval [b,d] becomes a tent function; λ₁, λ₂, … are pointwise orderings forming a Hilbert space that supports means, variances, and distances — a bridge to statistics and ML
The Euler characteristic curve χ(ε) = V − E + F tracks topological change through a filtration as a compact signature
The Reeb graph contracts each connected component of a level set of f: X→ℝ to a point; its nodes are topology-change (saddle) points — it is the theoretical basis of Mapper
visualizations: per-method tabs, all vanilla JS canvas 2D: Vietoris-Rips with ε-balls and cliques; Mapper (data+intervals → graph); Alpha complex (Delaunay with active simplices); persistence landscapes (tent functions + λ curves); Euler characteristic curve; Reeb graph with an animated level-set sweep
internal_tensions: Framing persistence landscapes as an ML/statistics bridge, yet never applying TDA to any neural network or learned embedding — a gap versus the math-for-AI cluster in this corpus
The Mapper clustering is a naive greedy distance-based clustering rather than the real Mapper's cluster-decomposition; the 'skeleton' is illustrative, not rigorous
All point sets are synthetic (clustered blobs, circle-with-flare); no real datasets are used

title: Sobolev-Räume W^{k,p}(Ω)
category_reason: Sobolev spaces and weak derivatives — functional analysis / PDE theory; ML appears only as one of eight applications (Sobolev training), not the focus
thesis: Sobolev spaces W^{k,p}(Ω) generalize the derivative via weak (distributional) derivatives, giving a rigorous home for the rough functions that arise as solutions of PDEs; their norm, hierarchy, and embedding theorems (Sobolev, Morrey) explain why enough derivatives force regularity.
key_claims: Weak derivative: v ∈ L^p is the weak derivative of u when ∫ u D^αφ = (−1)^|α| ∫ v φ for all test functions φ — the derivative is pushed onto smooth test functions via integration by parts
H^k = W^{k,2} is a Hilbert space with inner product Σ_{|α|≤k} ∫ D^αu D^αv, useful for projections, orthogonality, and the Riesz representation theorem
|x| ∈ W^{1,2}(−1,1) (weak derivative sign(x)) but ∉ W^{2,p} (second derivative 2δ(0), a distribution); Heaviside ∉ W^{1,p} (derivative δ(0)); |x|^{1/2} ∈ W^{1,p} only for p < 2 in 1D

Sobolev embedding: if kp < n then W^{k,p} ↪ L^q with Sobolev exponent q* = np/(n−kp); if kp = n (critical) it embeds into all L^q, q < ∞; if kp > n (Morrey) it embeds into C^{0,α} with α = k − n/p — enough derivatives force continuity
Lax–Milgram: the weak form ∫ ∇u·∇v = ∫ fv with coercivity a(u,u) ≥ α‖u‖² (via Poincaré) yields a unique weak solution u ∈ H₀¹ — the backbone of FEM and PDE existence
The Sobolev norm grows with frequency: higher ω in sin(ωπx) inflates ‖f'‖ and thus the H¹ norm — Sobolev norms measure smoothness by 'punishing' oscillation
Applications include heat/wave equations, elasticity, Navier–Stokes (Millennium problem), FEM, and — as one card — 'Sobolev training' of neural nets via Sobolev-norm regularization
visualizations: function & weak-derivative plot canvases (vanilla JS canvas 2D) for |x|, sin(πx), Heaviside, |x|^{1/2}, x·sin(1/x)
animated Sobolev-norm bars per derivative order; frequency-vs-H¹-norm plot
nested-ellipses function-space hierarchy; embedding-regime diagram (kp<n / =n / >n) with a position indicator
internal_tensions: A 'Machine Learning' application card (Sobolev training / Sobolev-norm regularization) sits alongside physics applications — an explicit math-for-AI hook, but thin and unelaborated versus the analysis focus
The 'forgiving teacher' analogy and the regime diagram are pedagogical; the file does not discuss the subtlety that the critical case is 'almost continuous but not continuous'

title: Also sprach Zarathustra – Interaktive Konzeptvisualisierung
category_reason: Interactive visualization of Nietzsche's Zarathustra concepts (Übermensch, eternal return, will to power); philosophy, no ML
thesis: An interactive gamification of Zarathustra's core concepts — the spirit's three metamorphoses, Übermensch vs. last man, eternal return, will to power, the transvaluation of values, and the death of God — turning Nietzsche's metaphysics into sliders, gauges, and mini-games.
key_claims: The spirit undergoes three metamorphoses: camel (carries the heaviest burden, 'you shall'), lion (fights the dragon 'you shall' to win freedom, 'I will'), child (innocent new creation, holy 'Yes')
The Übermensch is the meaning of the Earth and something humanity must overcome itself to become; the last man is the opposite — comfort, blinking, 'we have invented happiness,' no star
Eternal return (the 'greatest weight'): every joy and pain recurs infinitely; the test is whether you can say Yes to re-living your life eternally (the demon parable)
Will to power: life is not mere self-preservation but self-overcoming/growth; even in the servant's will one finds the will to be master
Transvaluation of all values: good and evil are human-made, not given from heaven; master-moral vs slave-moral; values must be continually re-created
The human is 'a rope, spanned between beast and Übermensch — a rope over an abyss'
The death of God leaves a vacuum to be filled by nihilism, the last man, the value-creator, or the Übermensch
visualizations: three-metamorphoses canvas path with burden bar (vanilla JS canvas 2D)

Plotly: Übermensch radar + gauge (chaos/overcoming/comfort/will-to-power), will-to-power growth-vs-resistance line, virtue bar chart (master vs slave moral), god-of-death radar scenarios, concept-network graph
animated eternal-return rotating event circle with spiral trail and 'Ja-Sagen'
interactive tightrope-balancing mini-game (mouse-controlled walker over an abyss)
internal_tensions: Quantifies Nietzsche with weighted scores (e.g. Übermensch = 0.25·chaos + 0.30·overcoming + 0.20·(100−comfort) + 0.25·will-to-power) — an instrumentalist flattening of concepts meant to resist quantification
Presents the 'last man' as a selectable persona rather than Nietzsche/Heidegger's existential diagnosis
The tightrope game treats the human-as-bridge as a balancing mechanic, reducing the 'dangerous crossing' to a skill task

title: Was heißt Denken? — Interactive Visual Exploration
category_reason: Interactive visualization of Heidegger's 'What Is Called Thinking?' (the four questions, the Twofold, Nietzsche, Parmenides); philosophy/phenomenology, no ML
thesis: A visually playful unpacking of Heidegger's Was heißt Denken (GA 8, 1951–52): the question of thinking splits into four modes, and what most calls for thinking withdraws while drawing us toward it — explored through the withdrawal paradox, Nietzsche's bridge over revenge, Parmenides' Geheiß, and the unthought Twofold of beings and Being.
key_claims: The question 'what is thinking?' unfolds into four: (1) what the word 'thinking' (Gedank) means; (2) what tradition has taken thinking to be (logic, λόγος, judgment); (3) what we must bring to think (a leap/readiness, not a method); (4) what calls us to think — the decisive, most thought-provoking question
The withdrawal that draws: what most calls for thinking withdraws from us, and this very withdrawal (Zug) is what draws us toward it — rendered as a slider paradox
Nietzsche's bridge: the Übermensch crosses from the 'last man' over the bridge of liberation from the spirit of revenge; the last man's will is revenge against time and its 'it was'
Revenge = the will's ill-will against time and its 'it was' (the frozen past); liberation is when the will wills the eternal return of the same — the will wills its own eternity

Parmenides' saying 'χρή τὸ λέγειν τε νοεῖν τ᾿ ἐὸν ἔμμεναι' is the Geheiß (command) that first called Western thinking into being; Heidegger re-reads each word etymologically (λέγειν = letting-lie-before, νοεῖν = taking-to-heart)
The Twofold (Zwiefalt) — the difference between beings (Seiendes) and Being (Sein) — is the unthought: all metaphysics moves within it yet never thinks it
Gedanc (heart/Gemüt) is the root of memory (Gedächtnis), remembrance (Andenken), thanks (Dank), and thinking (Denken)
visualizations: three.js 3D: Nietzsche's bridge (last-man platform → bridge → Übermensch platform over an abyss) and the Twofold (green beings-spheres + golden Being-tori + rose Zwiefalt particles, drag to rotate)
Plotly: four-questions radar, revenge time-spiral (3D), eternal-return polar, liberation bar, Parmenides sankey (λέγειν), Twofold polar, and a history-of-thought scatter (Parmenides → Heidegger)
vanilla JS canvas 2D: withdrawal paradox (human ↔ calling orb with pull lines), χρή concentric circles, νοεῖν heart, ἔμμεναι emerging waves, Gedanc word-network; hero particle field
internal_tensions: The page concedes it is 'not a substitute for the text' — acknowledging that Heidegger's thinking resists the visualization it performs
Uses a 'proximity to the Geheiß' y-axis for the history plot and numeric radar 'depth' scores — quantifying precisely what Heidegger says is unthought
A section is literally 'Nietzsche's Bridge,' tying this Heidegger piece to the Zarathustra visualization
